Set the minimum R version a package needs

Source: R/46_use_r_v4.1.0.R, R/47_use_r.R
use_r.Rd

use_r() scans the package sources for base R functions and syntax introduced in recent R versions, then records the highest version it finds in the Depends field of DESCRIPTION with usethis::use_package(). use_r_v4.1.0() is a shortcut that always requires R (>= 4.1.0), the version that introduced \() and |>.

use_r() detects:

  • R (>= 4.1.0): |>, \(), isa().

  • R (>= 4.2.0): the _ pipe placeholder in a named argument, Sys.setLanguage().

  • R (>= 4.3.0): the _ pipe placeholder heading an extraction chain.

  • R (>= 4.4.0): %||%, sort_by(), Tailcall(), Exec().

  • R (>= 4.5.0): use(), grepv(), the penguins dataset.

  • R (>= 4.6.0): %notin%, messageCondition(), match.arg(several.ok = "all"), barplot(orderH =).

Names that the package defines itself, such as its own %||%, never raise the requirement: they are reported and ignored. |>, \() and the _ placeholder are syntax rather than names, so they always count. A DESCRIPTION that already requires a higher version is never downgraded.

Usage

use_r_v4.1.0(path = NULL, ...)

use_r(path = NULL, dirs = c("R", file.path("tests", "testthat")), ...)

Arguments

path

Path to the package root. If NULL (the default), the current working directory is used.

...

Must be empty. Reserved for future arguments.

dirs

Package-relative directories scanned by use_r(). Defaults to "R" and "tests/testthat"; missing directories are ignored.

Value

use_r() invisibly returns the detected minimum R version, or NULL when nothing requires a recent R. use_r_v4.1.0() invisibly returns NULL, called for side effects.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tmpdir <- tempdir()
usethis::create_package(path = tmpdir)
use_r_v4.1.0(path = tmpdir)
use_r(path = tmpdir)
} # }
